evidence: Verified at frozen HEAD 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 against base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d. src/service/delivery_presentation.rs:62 and :306 unconditionally call std::sync::Mutex::lock before hook_presentation_view/watch_presentation_view can inspect CallBudget. The pull guard spans store.presentation_pull at :199 and post-store ledger/replay installation through :288; the confirmation guard similarly spans its store call. ModChannelRegistry::presentation_owner (src/service/mod_channels.rs:696-698) returns the same per-seat PresentationState permit used by registration/replacement (:827-831), and the fallback weak cache also reuses a live same-seat mutex. A valid second pull or confirmation already cancelled, or cancelled/deadline-expired while that mutex is held, cannot reach any budget check until the owner releases it. Rust's fetched primary documentation confirms lock's semantics: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Mutex.html#method.lock — 'Acquires a mutex, blocking the current thread until it is able to do so.' src/daemon/transport.rs:318-320 retains the ordinary admission permit for the function's lifetime; :516-533 cancels on expiry, socket activity/EOF or shutdown and then awaits the synchronous worker before returning. Therefore those waiters retain workers and ordinary slots after cancellation, potentially consuming the finite 32-slot pool (:31, :192) during a slow owner transaction. This is distinct from interrupting an accepted commit: src/store/connection.rs:330-336 explicitly accepts unbounded physical commit/fsync duration for the owner, not predecision waiting by other calls. The base and current src/store/mod.rs::writer (:355-385 current) use try_lock plus live_budget on every contention iteration, so waiting for another writer was already cancellable; the new presentation mutex bypasses that protection. The base has no delivery_presentation.rs or presentation owner permit. The owner-replay design section 2 requires holding the owner fence through canonical work/progress installation, while TRUST-POLICY.md:1714-1715 says the added finite allowances add no time-budget extension and weaken no cancellation; neither requires uninterruptible acquisition. I searched the named design documents and TRUST for cancellation, deadlines/time budgets, owner permits/mutexes, contention, blocking and commit/fsync exceptions. The accepted render/output/restart limits do not authorize this waiter behavior. This is a new significant cancellation/resource-release regression on Hook/Watch V2 pull and confirmation paths; cancellable acquisition can preserve the required exact-owner fence. Structural proof is sufficient; no runtime test was run.
